text: To improve our financial resilience as a nation, there is a need to plug the current financial literacy gap among Singaporeans and empower Singaporeans with the knowledge and confidence to take greater ownership of their financial well-being.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: First of all, I would like to suggest that the Government develop a National Financial Literacy Framework to provide a systematic basis for benchmarking improvements in financial literacy levels over time.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In the Financial Literacy Survey conducted by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) in 2005, a scoring system was mooted, covering both knowledge and action.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, it appears that the scoring system was discontinued in subsequent surveys.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Aggregate financial literacy statistics of Singaporeans should be established, measured and tracked as part of ascertaining Singapore’s financial resilience.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, I would like to suggest that the Government establish a National Financial Education Programme under MOE to provide proactive and comprehensive financial education for Singaporeans across all ages.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note that the Minister for Education had mentioned previously that financial literacy is infused into subjects such as Character and Citizenship Education (CCE), and that the Student Learning Space provides self-paced lessons for students to learn financial literacy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, I believe financial literacy is such a critical subject matter that we should not adopt a “by-the-way” approach.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Instead, we should equip Singaporeans across all ages with deeper financial knowledge and confidence.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This should include not just MoneySENSE’s Tier 1 knowledge of basic money management but should also aim to significantly improve Singaporeans’ financial capacity in Tier 2, which is financial planning, and Tier 3, investment knowhow.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Financial literacy should be included as a standalone subject taught in schools, as good financial habits need to be started from young.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It does not need to be an examinable subject.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Financial literacy clubs can be included as a co-curricular activity across all schools.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These clubs can also be set up at all community and SAFRA clubs, with structured activities.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Third, the concentration of household wealth in residential property assets needs to be addressed to give Singaporeans the financial freedom to explore other asset classes for their retirement planning in order to achieve better diversification and improve returns on their assets.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: A DBS report has indicated that property will no longer be the best retirement investment in Singapore in the future.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Having half of Singaporeans’ wealth in a single, relatively illiquid asset is a financial risk.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This could, in turn, better secure Singaporeans’ retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We need to move away from the over-emphasis on preparing for high stakes examinations, and place greater focus on enjoying learning and achieving subject and skills mastery.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Equipping Singaporeans with greater financial knowledge and confidence will enable them to take charge of their financial well-being and make better-informed decisions on their personal finances.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Strengthening Singaporeans’ financial resilience will also serve to enhance our overall resilience as a nation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Rational and responsible debate in Parliament that focuses on policies, not personalities, is the way to express our diverse views and improve our policies, with the objective of improving the lives of Singaporeans while remaining united as one people.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It may be defined as a system, organisation or society in which people are chosen for or occupy positions of success, wealth, power and influence on the basis of demonstrated ability and hard work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, it is a system in which there is a promise of reward in recognition of talent and industry.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This promise of reward has encouraged many Singaporeans to set ambitious targets for themselves to achieve as best they can in business as well as in the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This has driven our economy and has also attracted global talent to Singapore who have contributed tremendously to us becoming an international business hub.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Meritocracy continues to be relevant, and we should maintain it as Singapore's key societal organising principle.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: However, our form of meritocracy has also led to unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Second, intergenerational transfers of wealth threaten to create a permanent over-class which gives rise to inequity in access to opportunities.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: First, we should look at recognising the value of the work done by workers who work with their hands or who are in the practical professions.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I submit that we should leverage heavily on the existing and any upcoming Progressive Wage Model (PWM) sectors to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Raising wages will help to effect the shift in our definition of merit by showing that the work done by these workers, even if not generally considered work of the mind, is also important and will of the reward.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: For example, cleaners ensure the cleanliness of Singapore which is a distinctively Singaporean characteristic that contributes to our comfort and health and the aesthetics of our country.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is important work and it is often backbreaking work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: There is no reason why such work should be considered lesser than other work and less deserving of high reward.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We should also accelerate job redesign by incentivising employers.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: One way would be to modify the wage rungs in the existing PWMs such that each has a basic and an enhanced sub-realm.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In order to qualify for the enhanced sub-realm, workers must be trained in specific skills, for example, the use of technology.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In return, they will be entitled to a higher wage floor within that PWM realm.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Employers who hire more of these workers and pay at the higher rates could receive a progressive wage and hence, rung incentive.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This will encourage more employers to transform their businesses to upskill their workers and to offer more sophisticated services to their clients.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: There is already a Progressive Wage Credit Scheme but this payout is across the board for all wage increases.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Could we consider tweaking it so that it does not support all wage increases in the PWM sectors equally, but provides more support for the right types of wage increases?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This will help to improve our workers not only in terms of what they earn but also redesign their jobs from being largely manual to being higher skilled, uplifting how their jobs are perceived, as well as how they themselves feel about their professions.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Next, we can foster changes in mindset towards the practical professions by choosing our nomenclature carefully.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Instead of referring to these sectors as low-wage sectors, perhaps, we could consider referring to them as maybe emerging wage sectors or emerging wage workers.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The whole purpose of the PWM is to get these workers out of being low-wage earners.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But, if on the journey there, we keep referring to them as low-wage workers, we may unwittingly create a stigma that will stick even after we have lifted them from being low wage.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Second, I would like to propose that we also create opportunities in our education system for students to be exposed to the practical professions so that they can see and experience the work done by these sectors and learn to appreciate that all work is good work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, one day, we will see our students seeking internships or apprenticeships as technicians, arborists or waiters, and not just in law firms and banks.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Inheritance tax is a form of wealth tax and can be gradated so that it is progressive in nature; that is, the wealthier will be taxed more and would pay more.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The raison d'etre for this is that the rich presumably benefit more from state resources and also because progressive taxes act as a means to redistribute resources in society.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In principle, I do not think that many would dispute the principles behind wealth taxes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: However, we must be careful when designing and implementing any form of wealth tax so that we do not undo the features that underpin Singapore's success and prosperity in the first place.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must avoid becoming unattractive as a destination for foreign investment or to disincentivise our people from working hard and aspiring to grow their wealth.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, wealth taxes should not diminish the value of merit and should not affect our overall attractiveness as a business hub.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, inherited residential property is not taxed and does not even attract stamp duty.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: There should also be provision for beneficiaries to be able to pay the tax by instalments over a period of time.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Some would argue that some beneficiaries may not be able to afford the tax despite having inherited a multimillion-dollar property.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that they should sell the property to make payment of their dues to the Government.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: There are also mechanisms that an individual may take up, for example, life insurance that can cover any taxes that beneficiaries may have to pay after that individual has passed.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Why do I suggest an inheritance tax on property?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Estate duties tax the estate of a deceased person and, in my view, this could be seen as a form of double taxation because the deceased had already paid taxes while alive.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, inheritance is anyway not treated as a gift under the law.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It should be treated as a form of income received by the beneficiary and like all income, it should be taxed.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The basic principle, Sir, of meritocracy is that one should be rewarded for his capabilities and hard work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Inheritance provides rewards that are not pursuant to capability or hard work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: They are unmeritorious rewards that one is entitled to only by virtue of birth and/or bequeathment.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It does not stimulate innovation, entrepreneurship or industry.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, it entrenches entitlement and it promotes indolence.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Although it may be the impulse of parents to wish to provide for their children and to leave a legacy, inheritance, in my view, is a very antithesis of meritocracy.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: As a Scottish American industrialist, Andrew Carnegie said, "The parent who leaves his son enormous wealth generally deadens the talents and energies of the son and tempts him to lead a less worthy life than he otherwise would have." A large proportion of the wealthy at this point store their wealth in property.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And, as a form of investment, it is generally less helpful to society at large than other things of wealth, like capital or shares, which contribute to economic output as well as to employment.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Further to this, as for any text, we should also consider whether it would result in onerous administration and whether it is sustainable.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is therefore the lowest hanging fruit to promote equity and fairness and fair access to opportunities across generations based on merit.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This having been said, there are many serious considerations in whether it is appropriate to implement wealth and inheritance taxes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not something that we should rush into because it may itself have unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: But as the President said, as we prosper as a society, those who have already done well will seek to pass their advantages to their children, and this could lead to advantages and privileges becoming entrenched and persisting over generations.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Inheritance taxes are one measure we could consider implementing to battle this.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: I do not think that we should seek to build a classless society or that children should not be allowed to benefit from their parents' hard work.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: What we should aim to build is an inclusive society where capabilities and hard work in every sector are recognised and rewarded, and where, even when one attains success, he does not feel that he has become superior or be given the right to look down on others but feels responsibility to help others to advance as well.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must also take steps to prevent an entrenched overclass from forming by rich families building wealth over generations and scions benefiting from nothing but the hard work of their forebears.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: All must feel the need to work hard in Singapore in order to earn our rewards.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We must act on this; for if we do not, we risk descending from a meritocracy to an aristocracy and that, Sir, is what we must avoid at all costs.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Underpinning these is the strong foundation of trust that was demonstrated and strengthened through our shared experience during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), our vision is for "a better and more meaningful life where workers of all collars, ages and nationalities can work, live and play together in Singapore." And we achieve this through Singapore's unique brand of tripartism in which the Labour Movement stands shoulder to shoulder with our partners towards the shared objective of growing the economy, to secure better wages, welfare and work prospects for all workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the pandemic, our local businesses and workers were heavily impacted.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC worked closely with the Government to coordinate assistance programmes to protect lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Our support ranged from unions' ground efforts with companies to "cut costs to save jobs", to the provision of cash relief to union members and helping tens of thousands of workers with skills retraining and job placements.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: All these policies and programmes are not possible without the trust and value that tripartism had achieved over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As Prime Minister Mr Lee Hsien Loong had said in his speech at the May Day Rally 2018, "Tripartism has seen us through every crisis since Independence...

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Through our first major recessions, the oil crisis in 1970s, the major recession in 1985… It showed us through the Asian Financial Crisis, SARS and the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Each time, the challenges seemed daunting, sometimes even overwhelming.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But without the Labour Movement partnering companies, without the NTUC partnering the PAP in a symbiotic relationship, without the Government, unions and businesses sharing responsibility for Singapore's future, we would not have made it here." Tripartite trust built up over decades withstood many trials and tribulations in our young history and was strengthened after each and every crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: COVID-19 was no exception and we must continue to strengthen this trust that is the basis of tripartism going to the future.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Moving forward, the Labour Movement will persist in our efforts to protect the rights and to advance the interests and aspirations of all workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The future of work will have new sets of challenges and difficulties: ever-evolving geopolitics, technological advancements and disruptions and sociocultural shifts.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC will continue to renew and strengthen our compact with our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To do so, NTUC launched the #EveryWorkerMatters Conversations (#EWMC) last year to refresh our compact with our workers and to give greater assurance that we will journey with them, alongside them and to champion their cause.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Through the #EWMC, we have heard the voices of various groups of workers across all ages, sectors and backgrounds, and we will adjust our strategies to meet their needs and their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I will now share three main areas that NTUC will focus on going forward: (a) expand career opportunities; (b) enhance assurance and protection; and (c) ensure career resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The CPM was a continuation of what the NTUC Secretary-General said previously in 2020, and again in 2021, about professionalising the solar technologists and plumbers respectively through a Career Development Plan.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: However, there is also a growing concern of a “skilled trades gap” as the older generation retires, coupled with the lack of qualified candidates to step up to fill the gaps.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC wants to ensure a sustainable supply of locals into these trades to meet our national needs.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Supporting these workers is also part of our social compact to be a more inclusive society, where we do not just recognise cognitive skills but also technical and hands-on skills.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Another key group that we set out to engage is youths.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Youths today are faced with a more competitive education and employment landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: At the height of COVID-19 when there were limited jobs, the SGUnited Traineeships Programme has been a tremendous help.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: But NTUC thinks that our younger workers, embarking on the first steps in their careers, will need more support.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We want our future workforce to be able to dream big, aspire high and achieve their fullest potential in whatever they wish to do in a wide range of career opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas will be happy to hear that we will be partnering many Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to allow a lot more opportunities for our young undergraduates in this area of work.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC’s networks with industry and with workers of different cohorts make us well placed to link them up with internship opportunities and career mentors across different sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We will share more on our plans over the next few months.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The second area of focus is to enhance career assurance and protection.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We want to support our workers with their immediate concerns in tackling higher cost of living and also in addressing mid- to longer-term issues of job security, unemployment support, retirement adequacy and also caregiver support.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: For our lower-wage workers, the Labour Movement has been actively pushing for more workers to be covered under the PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We have made much progress in uplifting lower-wage workers and will continue to press on to cover all sectors and to implement PWM in good time.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Our mid-career workers, especially those above 40 years of age, are another segment of workers who are very vulnerable to industry disruptions and restructuring.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: My fellow Labour Member of Parliament Mr Patrick Tay has been championing for unemployment support and protection in Parliament since as early as 2014 and on several other occasions in the House, and I am sure he will continue to push for it through the PME Taskforce proposal that was finalised in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC also recognises that more protections should be accorded to our freelance and self-employed workers, including our platform workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The recent announcement on work injuries compensation, improving housing and retirement adequacy, and enhancing representation is a welcomed move.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We will continue to work closely with the tripartite partners to see through the implementation and to further strengthen their representation.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Our senior workers should also be tapped upon and valued for their experience and their industry knowledge.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Our workers must also be assured that they are able to achieve basic retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We want to look into how we can better support them to reduce the mental and emotional load on caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The third area of focus for NTUC is to ensure career resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As the global job market evolves, our workers will experience change and disruption over their lifetime in their career.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: And this increases the importance of career resilience and upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: To plan for a longer horizon, NTUC will support our workers to handle career changes by developing new and deepening existing skills to stay relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: I have also called for increased financial support and protected training time to enable workers to acquire deeper skillsets throughout their careers, or equip themselves to pivot to new areas.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Going forward, this is an area that will need support from all tripartite partners to ensure our workers’ skillsets remain relevant and our businesses have adequate workers to sustain our future economy.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: With the acceleration of digital and green economy, it is imperative for companies to plan ahead, to capitalise key trends and transform their businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Through CTCs, NTUC will support companies to do all that, plus redesign jobs, upskill and reskill workers and collectively achieve greater business and workers’ outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, in order to better understand the aspirations of our workers and better serve them, NTUC has rolled out the #EveryWorkerMatters Conversations that lasted for one year, starting from August last year.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Through more active communication with our workers, we want to work together with them to create a better future.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: NTUC will focus on three key areas in our future work: first, help workers to capture economic opportunities in the future; second, protect our workers' interest; and third, increase the career resilience of our workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: First, NTUC will help workers capture opportunities in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We hope that through the Career Progression Model, we can encourage more Singaporeans to enter craftsman and related trades such as plumbing, electrical works and air-conditioning maintenance and master a skill.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: This will also ensure the continuous development of these industries.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We also need to ensure that our youth and young workers, no matter what economic situation our country is in, will be able to find suitable jobs, use their skills and contribute to our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: Second, NTUC will continue to protect our workers’ interests.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the short term, NTUC will help our workers address higher cost of living; in the medium to longterm, NTUC will help address urgent issues including providing better jobs, unemployment insurance, retirement adequacy and care support.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As the global economy and technology continues to advance, workers between the ages of 40 and 50 will continue to face higher risk of being unemployed or replaced.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: The Government, during the pandemic, has rolled out many programmes to help our workers retain their jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In the future, NTUC will work together with the Government to expand our programme to help more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: These will better represent the interests of our freelancers and self-employed workers.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We must encourage our workers to continue to upskill and strengthen their competitiveness and adaptability in the new environment.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We hope that with more enterprises joining this programme, more workers would be able to master future-ready skills and companies can enjoy stronger competitiveness too.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: We want to help our workers to find a job that they are proud of, protect their livelihood and create a brighter future with quality jobs and lives.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, in Singapore, generations of Government and NTUC leaders have worked hard to uphold personal integrity and trust in every aspect.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: And the dividends can clearly be seen in the way we have navigated through the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: However, we must be vigilant to always nurture this trust because we are not immune to what is happening around us and around the world.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: As shared by Mr Lee Kuan Yew at a mass rally in Geylang Serai in 1959 and, thereafter, repeated at the NTUC’s 50th Anniversary Dinner in 2011, and I quote, “In Government, I have never forgotten that it is in the interests of workers and their unions that we must strive for growth and development.

speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
text: In other words, growth is meaningless unless it is shared by the workers, shared not only directly in wage increases but indirectly in better homes, better schools, better hospitals, better playing fields and, generally, a healthier environment for families to bring up their children.” The President Address last week sets out the Government’s plans to achieve just that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.50 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.32 pm until 3.50 pm.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I likened it to the Lego bricks that my son loves to play with.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, at the core of its structure, each brick must be strong.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is the family unit and each of us, fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, the interlocking connection between each brick must be strong.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is our social cohesion that makes building something bigger than ourselves not just possible but also durable in the long run.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, the different shapes and sizes of each Lego brick not only complement one another but also when combined makes them unique and vibrant.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is our multiracial and multi-religious society that makes Singapore rich not only in culture but also diverse in views and expertise.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is why I resonate with the Address of the President, which reiterates the Government's commitment to strengthen our basic building blocks – our families and fellow Singaporeans – by holding on to our core values of fairness, inclusivity, mutual support and giving back to society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These values were embodied in the many success stories of our everyday Singaporeans working together with the Government, the community and the businesses to help all of us get through the pandemic together.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For me, President Halimah's speech not only presented the Government's priorities and plans in the coming period, but it also acknowledged how we managed to overcome the pandemic and its challenges together as one society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The President's speech also reminded us that we face an important challenge to ensure that there remains continued trust between the political leadership and our people and between all of us fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is not to say that we have to be monolithic or homogenous in our views and approach.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need courageous Singaporeans who are brave enough to experiment things differently, who dare to speak up and are willing to stand up for the issues that matter to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Inevitably, this part of the nation-building process means that there will necessarily be divergent views – each with its own benefits and trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The rigour of debates and contestation of ideas on issues that are important to Singaporeans can help all of us formulate new ways forward for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, at the same time, such discussions must be done respectfully and responsibly, based on facts and on honest terms.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Whether these discussions are in the halls of this House or in the comfort of our homes, we can hold different opinions but we must believe in the same vision for the betterment of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This must be our pillar of strength – our unity in diversity regardless of race, religion or political inclinations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Through the Forward Singapore conversations, the Government's call to involve various stakeholders – employers, workers, community partners, civil society and, indeed, all Singaporeans – in our nation-building means that we would be able to tap on our nation's greatest resource; not our Reserves but each other's strengths and expertise.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must unlock our collective spirit to help one another.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is the principle of social solidarity where the people, through its government, bear equally the responsibility and burden for helping fellow citizens.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The task of helping the underprivileged or vulnerable in our society does not fall on the shoulders of the Government or civil society alone but on all of us.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But how do we maintain such social cohesion and solidarity?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Just like the Lego bricks, we need to strengthen the interlocking connections that bind us and guard against threats and external forces that seek to divide us and undermining our painstakingly built level of trust in the institutions of our nation and society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Externally, we must continue to remain vigilant and ensure our laws keep up to date with global trends, threats and developments.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Internally, we must remain steadfast and committed to our Singaporean values of living in an open but multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The pandemic has laid bare the vulnerabilities of societies all over the world.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Global studies have found that there is a correlation between the pandemic and explicit xenophobic and racial prejudices.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Anti-discrimination or legislative guards against hate speech go some way but we also need a softer approach for a more enduring harmony.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I look forward to the Government's plans to ensure that our laws remain relevant in maintaining our social and racial harmony.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will complement the existing Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act passed since 1990.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This understanding and appreciation of one another's values and cultures is the key towards breaking the cycle of ignorance and racism.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope that the law will also offer protection to whistle-blowers who report such instances of racial prejudices and unfair employment practices.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides protection and safeguards on our social cohesion, we also need ways to promote social solidarity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree with the President that as we strive for success and progress for our nation, we must not allow our society to stratify into those who have and those who are left behind.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need to build a sense of collective responsibility among us.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must appreciate the interdependence between people in our society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must make Singaporeans feel that they can improve the lives of others and, in the same process, uplift their own lives in a meaningful way.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In adulthood and working life, we see more businesses – both employers and employees – dedicate more pro bono hours towards corporate social responsibility activities on various causes that are beneficial to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must continue to promote and incentivise this "paying it forward" as part of our working culture here in Singapore and truly understand that there is no contradiction between doing what is best for the company and doing what is good for the community and nation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The President also emphasised that in paying it forward, we must help one another to stand tall with dignity and pride.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This means that it is not patronising from the perspective of the person receiving.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is a work in progress and we must continue to refine the approach and solutions in a targeted yet dignified and respectful manner without converting the social mobility ladder into a crutch of help that will be both belittling and debilitating.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must continue to keep a close eye on areas that will affect the social harmony and justice for the vulnerable groups in our society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   In my view, President Halimah's speech not only lays out the Government's priorities and future plans, but it also acknowledges how we managed to overcome the pandemic together as one people.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At the same time, however, the President's speech recognised that the key challenge is to ensure that there was continued trust between the political leadership and our people and between Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our pillars of strength are peace and unity in diversity regardless of race, religion or political views.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree that the approach and discussion of issues that concern our people and community should be discussed respectfully, responsibly, factually and judiciously.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I agree that generally, for issues that are important to our country, many of us place national interests above individual rights.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, this is not always guaranteed and the critical challenge for all of us is to prioritise social cohesion and our country’s progress in an ever-changing post-pandemic world.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Let us respond to the call for unity to ensure that while we achieve progress for our people and country, we do not overlook those who are in greater need so that they are not engulfed in the tide of modernity and change.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We should not leave them behind because if everyone does not experience happiness and progress, our social fabric will be incomplete and imperfect – as the Malay proverb goes, it will be like an unfinished dress because the thread ran out and the needle broke.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, as our society grows through decades of nation-building, we have built a sense of identity and belonging as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, who qualifies as a member of our society should not be narrowly defined and we should not be quick to succumb to the othering phenomenon and the pitting of "us" versus "them" – whatever "us" and "them" mean.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The fault lines in our society can be easily exploited, knowingly or unknowingly, through the differences in how we look, where we come from, whether or not we can speak a certain language, whether we belong to the same social standing or whether we agree or disagree on a particular policy.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: SG50, SG Together, SGUnited, SG Cares – all of these campaigns are reminders of what we can achieve when we remain united in our hearts and minds.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Let us continue to stand with one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After three years of the COVID-19 crisis, we now confront other formidable challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as we have seen again and again in our history, we can find opportunities in every crisis and move quickly to take advantage of them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are stark realities facing Singapore and the wider world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From the war in Europe to deepening big power rivalry in our part of the world, we all feel a palpable sense of danger – danger not just to the economy, but also to an open and stable global order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to be afflicted by these external headwinds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know many Singaporeans worry about the unexpected twists and turns that may lie ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of the support has been given out, while others will be rolled out progressively over the year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have and will continue to do everything we can to address the stresses and strains that people feel on the ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides tackling the cost of living, sustaining growth will be more challenging in this new environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to redouble our efforts to attract investments and talent, and create good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to intensify the pace of restructuring and transformation to stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this will not be easy, but COVID-19 has shown that Singaporeans have what it takes – the grit and resolve to overcome tough challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The odds may appear stacked against us, but we can turn challenges into opportunity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With pride in our history and strength from our unity, we can forge ahead with confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will build on our strong foundations, but we must also have the courage to change where change is needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is what my colleagues and I have set out to do with Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through this exercise, we are reviewing our policies across all areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will ensure that the broad middle of society and their children see continued improvements in their lives, and that we close the gaps for the more disadvantaged groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have heard from Singaporeans over the past months – your views, aspirations and ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The many conversations and partnerships have yielded fresh insights on what we can do differently in our next stage of nation-building.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we succeed in effecting these shifts, we can secure a stronger social compact and not just among ourselves, but between this generation and future generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want every child to have a strong foundation that can propel them forward through life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the age of three, we are stepping up the provision of MOE Kindergartens and Government-funded preschools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Enrolment in preschool at ages five to six is already near universal, but the attendance rate of children from lower-income families can still be improved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At ages three to four especially, more children from such families can also benefit from enrolling in preschool.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will study how to strengthen their participation in these early years of development, so that we can give the children in these families the best possible start in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Once our children enter the school system, there is a comprehensive system in place to help them develop and grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already provide more resources in our schools to support children with greater learning needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will continue to do more on this front, so that every child can realise his or her full potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is a deeper challenge in our education system: our concept of meritocracy remains too narrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many feel caught in a rat race from a young age – under pressure to get the best grades, get into what they perceive to be the best schools so that they can get the best university places.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many parents, too, are anxious about their children's future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some go to great lengths to maximise their children's chances to get into perceived brand name schools, even preschools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A decade ago, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat said that "Every school is a good school”.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because in Singapore, everyone can be assured that, no matter which schools their children are admitted into, they will receive a good education, and they will be well supported by their teachers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I went to the primary and secondary schools near my home and reaped the full benefits of learning in those schools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the quality of our schools and teachers has improved dramatically since.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These days, our teachers do not just focus on content and knowledge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They help our children to think independently and instil in them qualities and values that contribute to lasting success in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remember, at the end of the day, we are more than our grades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are more than the schools we go to.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is an aspiration Singaporeans have voiced for some time now, from when we held Our Singapore Conversation a decade ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since then, we have made significant moves and slayed some sacred cows.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In their place, there is full Subject-based Banding (SBB).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We hope these moves will go some way to remove the stressors in our education system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But more importantly, we hope they will signal to all in society that we are serious about refreshing our system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope that our society too – every man, woman and child, young and old, rich or poor – all of us will be serious about refreshing our mindsets about schools and grades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not possible to change something that has become so ingrained in our nature by government decree.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must be the change we want to see in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every Singaporean must want to give themselves and their children more breathing space to discover and develop their diverse talents and to maximise their potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key mindset shift is to recognise that formal education early in life is not the endpoint of our meritocracy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our refreshed meritocracy must be a continuous one, with learning opportunities, milestones and ladders at multiple junctures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All must have the chance to try again, do better and move forward in life, years after leaving school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the skills journey begins in schools but it does not end with schools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our new approach on skills must include a fresh commitment to making continuous learning, reskilling and upskilling a way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, this will become more important with slower economic growth, rapid technological disruptions and greater job churn.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To remain an upwardly mobile society, lifelong learning will be key – not just upskilling once and being done with it, but multiple times, to become more adaptable and resilient, well-equipped and confident to face the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To get there, education cannot be confined to the first 25 years of our lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Learning must be a lifelong journey for the whole of our lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We aim to reduce the costs and lower the barriers to training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will work with industry partners to come up with effective training programmes, including work-based learning options.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These courses will have to be better curated and vetted so that they translate into meaningful employment outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will discuss with tripartite partners how we can support workers to take time off to train.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help the workers individually, but it will help businesses too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, businesses must shift their emphasis from hiring credentials to hiring skills and invest in the development of their employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And Singaporeans themselves must be open to change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nur Afifah Bte Rakif graduated with a Diploma in Communication and Information Design 11 years ago, when she was 22.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She later chose to teach in a preschool in 2013, took up various early childhood education programmes to reskill and upskill, and became the Deputy Centre Lead of the NTUC First Campus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To strengthen her skillsets, she is now pursuing a degree under the Singapore University of Social Science (SUSS) Work-Study Programme and will graduate later this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Afifah exemplifies the spirit of lifelong learning and the value of reskilling and upskilling in pursuing one's passions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this new approach on skills, how well you did in school should not define the opportunities you can unlock nor should it determine your entire life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You are not stuck at your highest formal educational level attained; you can update your skillsets, pivot to new careers, seize new opportunities and keep moving forward in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some other nations aspire to create a welfare society from cradle to grave.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will aspire to create in Singapore a full-fledged learning society – from cradle to grave.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we will become a people ready for the future and equipped to succeed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Naturally, it means different things to different people, in different places.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Yet somehow, as a society, we tend to converge around a few material definitions – the size of the paycheck or the property we own.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How can we shift our lens and collectively adopt and embrace wider definitions of success?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After all, success is really for each one of us to define.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We should not feel pressured to compare with others or to conform to preconceived notions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Japanese talk about discovering your "ikigai" – something that gives you a sense of purpose and joy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We should strive to be a meritocracy where everyone can be the best possible version of themselves and where there are many ways for diverse talents to contribute and earn respect in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mindset shifts are necessary, but I do not think mindset shifts alone will effect societal change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not enough to say we will celebrate a variety of professions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economic structures, remuneration and career prospects in various professions must also be consistent with what we value.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will consider ways to tilt the scales and narrow the wage gap across professions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Why not enable them to attain accreditation for their skills and set a clearer progression ladder as they take on greater responsibilities?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can ascribe the right values to such forms of labour and grant such workers greater remuneration as professionals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More broadly, we also want to give Singaporeans who graduate from ITE and polytechnics stronger assurance; that their wages and career prospects will not be too far below their university-going peers and will not be permanently conscribed to be below.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, they do not have to succumb to a paper chase to secure a good salary and a viable career path.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They can excel in the professions that they have trained in and have the aptitude for, be it hospitality, infocomm, social services or others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many ways to make a difference, many talents to nurture and many forms of contributions to reward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot close the gap altogether between lower-wage and median workers, but we can certainly stop their wages from diverging too far.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Here, I have a plea to everyone: for a new definition of success to become a reality, all of us – as consumers – must be willing to bear a higher cost for the goods and services we consume.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must recognise the important work that our fellow citizens undertake to keep our society going and do our part to uplift them and boost their wage prospects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know this is not an easy ask, given the rising cost of living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will do our best to manage the pace of change and to help everyone, especially our lower- and middle-income families, adjust to this new environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I might add too – all will gain when even the most vulnerable among us become better off.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will become a better people, a more just and a more equal society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a more uncertain world, we must also relook our approach on social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How can we assure both the broad middle and the vulnerable that they can meet their needs in life and not fall by the wayside or be left behind?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the vulnerable, we have been gradually shifting our approach from social assistance to social empowerment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want not only to help people tide through difficulty, but also to boost their sense of drive and purpose, and strengthen their sense of agency and ownership over their own circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, today, we have the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to help second-timer lower-income families, like Mr Gan and his wife Mdm Chai, own a home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The two of them work as cleaners and they lived in a rental flat in Redhill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they were determined to buy a home of their own for themselves and their young daughter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the Gans are proud owners of a 2-room flexi flat in Bukit Batok.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They collected their keys two months ago and just moved in earlier this month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their daughter is very excited about getting to decorate her own space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And over the next five years, our officers will continue to walk alongside them and give them the support they need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme is, in effect, a means to uplift and empower the vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to expand this approach of empowerment to cover more forms of social assistance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For instance, we could provide additional financial help to vulnerable families who do their part to help themselves, such as staying gainfully employed and sending their children to preschool regularly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the more a family takes ownership of their goals, the more we will help you to reach even higher – a mutually reinforcing, virtuous circle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also want to consider another group: persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do more to alleviate the impediments they face in life and adopt new ways of caring for and empowering them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Equally important is to empower persons with disabilitiesPwDs when they reach adulthood.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will involve and enable them to contribute to society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The onus is on all of us to find ways to affirm the dignity of our differently-abled citizens and enable them to realise their full potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore must never succumb to the kind of harsh inequality we see in so many other parts of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However treacherous the terrains ahead, so long as Singapore continues to progress, all Singaporeans must continue to progress, with none among us left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: No less important in our social strategy is to assure the broad middle that they, too, can be confident of meeting their needs at every stage of life, even in the face of setbacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Housing, education and healthcare – these are basic needs for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This Government has delivered on all these fronts over the decades and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have tightened the rules, so that flats go to those who need them most, as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we are doing more to help younger married couples and parents own their first home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will get this work done and we will deliver the results.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Affordable and accessible public housing will always be a key pillar of our social compact under the PAP Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our approach to social support also extends to how we will support our people in the face of setbacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a more volatile jobs landscape, we can expect more among us to be displaced from time to time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we help the unemployed through schemes like ComCare and the COVID-19 Recovery Grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They provide timely assistance while upholding our ethos of work and self-reliance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also know that losing a job is a major setback, which can easily destabilise workers and their families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the Government will consider doing more to support our displaced workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We intend to make this shift in our social strategy, so every Singaporean can be confident.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this harsh, unpredictable world, we will have your back and we will support you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will cheer you on, so you can strive to achieve, do your best and bounce back stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Strengthening our assurances extends to caring for our seniors too – this is an urgent need, given our rapidly ageing demographics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must adopt a new approach to care for our seniors well and in a sustainable way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We embarked on Healthier SG recently to care for our seniors upstream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Healthier SG signals a shift from treating illnesses to promoting health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we can help our seniors stay healthy, we will reduce the need for medical intervention and hospitalisation downstream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But care for seniors goes beyond physical health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our seniors age, we want them to be cared for in their own homes for as long as possible, rather than in a nursing home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This way, they can remain active and purposeful in their golden years, surrounded by family, friends and familial activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do all this and more, so we can create a home truly for our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our seniors must also be confident of meeting their retirement needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We achieve this through our CPF system, which we will continue to evolve and update.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will study enhancing these schemes to better support our seniors, including those nearing retirement who have less runway to work and save.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For younger Singaporeans, as long as you work and contribute to your CPF consistently, we will ensure that your needs in old age can be met through CPF.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And for those who do not have the ability to work, we will find other ways to look after your retirement needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is our promise to Singaporeans of every generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was our sense of collective responsibility that saw us through the pandemic, and it is the same sense of collective responsibility that will carry us through our next bound.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A social compact is not just about what Government will do for the people; it is also about what Singaporeans will do for one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, our refreshed social compact is not just about the Government doing more and Singaporeans depending more on the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Rather, it is about the Government, businesses, unions, workers, the community and civil society all doing their part for fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about all of us coming together, to forge a society of opportunities and assurance for everyone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One way to realise this is to nurture a broader culture of philanthropy and volunteerism: where we take responsibility for each other and especially to help those with less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This goes beyond money, it includes investing time and effort in nurturing others – from mentoring the young to providing those from disadvantaged circumstances with access to networks and opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another way is to create more opportunities for Singaporeans to partner the Government and one another in policy-making and co-creation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to involve Singaporeans and other groups in co-designing and shaping our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will provide more avenues and platforms for our youth to come up with policy ideas and build the future Singapore, for they are Singapore's future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will never stop investing in our urban infrastructure, developing our HDB towns by providing more facilities and amenities, and making concerted efforts to become a City in Nature.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But ultimately, it is up to all of us to contribute their own passions and energies to turn this city into an endearing home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Becoming the best home is also very much about the intangibles – among them, embracing a more holistic way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This project of making a better Singapore has always been, and will always be, a work in progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been a relentless effort over the decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will never stop improving, not just for ourselves but also for future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This ethos of building for the future, rather than burdening or weighing down our descendants, is key to Singapore's success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The prudence of the previous generation has enabled us to find our way through the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must do the same for those who come after us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us steward our resources well, so that our children and grandchildren will be well-endowed and well-prepared to tackle any challenge the future may bring – be it the climate crisis, the next pandemic, or the unknown unknowns which will come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the next few days of the debate, my colleagues will elaborate further on specific aspects of the agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, what do these shifts to our social compact mean?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, some ask, has the 4G team shifted to the left?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our governing approach is not so easy to characterise along the traditional political spectrum of left and right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After all, we have always strived to appeal to a broad base of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have always taken care not to base our legitimacy on any narrow social group or class.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also do not blindly copy or replicate the models of other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even the first generation of PAP leaders, who began their political lives as democratic socialists, spoke of a "Socialism that Works" – for they did not want any part of what they already knew was failing in Europe and elsewhere.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The countries with more welfarist policies, in continental Europe and the Nordics have much higher levels of state-financed welfare provisions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To fund such high spending, they impose high income taxes, usually much higher than 30%, even for the middle-income groups, with Value-added Tax (VAT) or Goods and Services Tax (GST) taxes ranging from 20% to 25%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we will chart our own way forward, staying true to our core values.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we will indeed do more to strengthen social safety nets, we will move with prudence and discipline, and not end up inflicting heavy tax burdens on everyone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, our overall tax burden for the middle-income group is far lower than other advanced nations and we will strive to keep it that way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More than that, we will ensure that our programmes achieve better outcomes for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we are already doing better than many other countries in areas like healthcare, education and housing; doing better not in terms of how much we spend, but in terms of outcomes – the value that we achieve from every dollar of public spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are doing better and we can keep on doing better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the spirit and intent behind the shifts we are considering – be it skills and continuous learning, social empowerment, active ageing and retirement adequacy, or housing assurances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes will benefit Singaporeans from every walk of life – they will uplift the vulnerable and also advance the well-being of our broad middle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, among the more advanced nations, Singapore is one of the few where people in the middle have experienced large increases of incomes in the last 20 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to sustain real income growth for the middle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why economic growth is non-negotiable for us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already know that our growth rates will gradually come down as our labour force expands more slowly and becomes older, but growth remains essential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we do not grow the economic pie, there will be fewer jobs and less scope for social support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This Government will and must always be pro-growth and pro-inclusivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
