text: We have merely sought to advance the interest of our Singaporean workers and to give voice to their persistent anxieties and concerns over our immigration policy and their livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is dangerous for the Government to misconstrue our concerns as being motivated by nativism, xenophobia and racism.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this session of Parliament, let us live up to the President's exhortation last week – for us to have constructive, respectful and responsible political debates that are based on facts and sound analysis.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the end of the day, we are all doing our best for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And a Parliament that is a fair arena for all parties is one that will earn further respect from its people.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To be effective in restoring the balance in our local job market and levelling the playing field for Singaporeans, the PSP thinks that we need policies with hard targets – like the ones PSP has proposed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We hope that the Government will continue to strengthen support for the unemployed and underemployed workers and raise the wages of low-income Singaporeans at a faster rate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP has proposed a minimum living wage to do this.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We also look forward to contributing to the debate on the new workplace fairness law next year.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have also pushed for improvement of the financial security of Singaporeans, which is most affected by the affordability and accessibility of public housing.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We had a substantive debate on this issue for some 12 hours in February, initiated by Ms Hazel Poa and me.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The public housing debate is yet another example that shows the value of having Opposition Members in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have reflected an issue that many Singaporeans are deeply concerned about, advanced Singaporeans' interest and aired their doubts on the Government's narrative about affordable housing in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have researched and thought through these policies before raising them in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are rational alternatives that we believe will better achieve our desired outcomes of affordable housing and family formation, while delinking retirement adequacy from housing prices.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I welcome the Government to provide statistics to substantiate their rhetoric that our alternative policies will cause a crash in the housing market.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: During this Session of the 14th Parliament, we will continue to scrutinise the Government's housing policies and keep a check on the Government's move to stabilise prices in the housing market.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In particular, Singaporeans are anxious to know what solutions the Government has, to resolve the lease-decay problem.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We will continue to ask the questions that Singaporeans want to ask, but may not be asked by Members of the ruling party.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That is our duty as a responsible and rational Opposition party.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We will also continue to put up alternative housing policies that we believe will be in the interest of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As always, we expect that these policies will be robustly challenged by the Government, but, we hope that these policies will not simply be brushed off as raiding the Reserves or crashing the housing market just because they do not fit into the Government's framework for the reserves of finances or challenge the Government's "sacred cow" policies, like homeownership.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope that the Government can refrain from such posturing, so that we can have a more productive debate in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Like I mentioned earlier, a fair arena for one and all.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: During her Address in 2020, the President said, as masters of our own land, Singaporeans must have confidence in their rights and privileges of citizenship.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Last week, the President spoke about deepening Singaporeans' sense of shared identity.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All Singaporeans should identify with the notion that we are masters of our own land and our shared identity should be grounded in the rights and privileges of citizenship.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP welcomes foreigners to complement the Singaporean Core.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But first and foremost, the PSP will do all it can to protect the position of Singaporeans, as masters of our own land.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP understands and empathises with many Singaporeans, who feel like they are second-class citizens in Singapore today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singaporeans feel like they are draining their resources just to stay afloat, instead of being empowered to swim towards a better life.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Naturally, they feel resentment when they see an influx of wealthy new immigrants setting up family offices and driving up property and Certificate of Entitlement (COE) prices.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: During my walkabouts, many Singaporeans have expressed to me that they are aggrieved that many naturalised Singaporean Citizens, who have arrived in Singapore comparatively recently, enjoy most of the benefits of citizenship and can gain from the resources that past generations of Singaporeans have accumulated, without having to serve National Service or even volunteer service in the SAF Volunteer Corps.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Eighteen-year-old Singaporeans make immense contributions to us being masters of our own land, by serving National Service.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is also the stance of the Workers' Party and Ms Sylvia Lim had just reiterated that in her speech today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In addition, we must do more to prioritise Singaporeans and redistribute economic gains, so that these perceptions can be corrected and we can empower those Singaporeans who feel like second-class citizens today.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the labour market, the interests of Singaporeans must be prioritised.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP will continue to fight for all these during this session of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We hope the Government will notice our serious alternative proposals this time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Meritocracy is a core value that has been instrumental to our nation's success.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is the principle that individuals should be rewarded based on their abilities and achievements, regardless of their background.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It has driven Singapore's economic growth and helped create a prosperous, inclusive and diverse society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, we must also recognise that meritocracy is not a perfect system and I am glad Mdm President touched on this.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is important to acknowledge the role that socioeconomic factors and perceived structural inequalities can play in limiting opportunities for certain groups.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: To address these challenges, we must continue to promote our brand of meritocracy that ensures everyone has the tools they need to succeed and one that has a broad definition of success.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And this is where education plays a crucial role: in not only being a vehicle of social mobility but providing multiple platforms for individuals with different interests and passion to develop.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This will, in turn, foster equal opportunities for all.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In our pursuit of meritocracy, we must continually invest in early childhood education to provide a strong foundation for our children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Early childhood is a critical period in which cognitive, social and emotional skills develop rapidly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By nurturing these skills from a young age, we can ensure that every child has an equal opportunity to succeed, regardless of background or circumstances.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In the fervent words of my maiden speech, I implored that we enshrine early childhood education as a fundamental right, a conviction I hold steadfastly to this day.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For me, this transcends the mere number of children attending school; it represents a profound transformation in our collective consciousness, a shift that underscores the indispensable value of making education not just accessible but unequivocally compulsory.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: MOE has championed this cause by offering diverse educational opportunities to cater to our student's unique strengths and interests.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the years, I have had students from various educational backgrounds in the polytechnic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Some came from the ITE, others through the Polytechnic Foundation Programme – they are actually "N" level students – and some were "A" level students, who decided to switch.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Regardless of their background, I have seen them doing very well when pursuing their diploma in polytechnics – partly due to them pursuing their field of interest.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Some continue to pursue their degrees afterwards, while others are in a job where their interests match.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As an educator, all I want is for my students to develop at their own pace and fulfil their passion and potential; and I have yet to be disappointed.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is a testament to our education system, which has evolved over the years to accommodate diverse interests and learning styles, foster creativity and promote critical thinking.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: One of my former students, Ibrahim, switched from the A-level route to do a diploma.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He came from a humble background and faced some challenges in his educational journey.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What stood out was that he was positive, hardworking and a natural leader – traits that go beyond grades.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: After a few years, he secured a place in university and landed a fulfilling job in his field of choice.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Ibrahim's story is a testament to the power of education and the opportunities it can provide.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this rapidly evolving world, our education system must adapt and innovate to foster well-rounded individuals who can thrive in diverse environments.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Ultimately, we, as a society, must recognise that success is not just about grades but also about developing character, values and life skills.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By shifting our focus to this holistic approach, we can empower our youths to become resilient, adaptable and compassionate leaders of tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our society has made great strides in recent years, recognising mental health as a critical aspect of our overall well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We have seen public awareness campaigns challenging stigma and, most importantly, more people stepping forward to seek help.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We must continue our efforts to destigmatise mental health, recognising that it is as important as our physical health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We have a collective responsibility to create an environment where everyone can access the support they need, without fear of judgement or discrimination.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government has recently invested in various initiatives to promote mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Additionally, The Mental Well-being Circles must be adequately and rigorously trained and deployed to provide that much-needed first tier of support in the community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By providing mental health education in schools and the IHLs and equipping dedicated staff with the necessary skills and resources, we can identify and support students at risk of developing mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Lastly, we must continue to fund and increase funding for mental health research.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Research not only helps us identify factors contributing to mental health issues, but also informs the creation of effective prevention and intervention strategies.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Additionally, research findings can guide the improvement of mental health services and the development of policies and programs tailored to individuals' needs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As we strive to create a brighter future for Singapore, let us remember that mental health is not an issue that can be resolved overnight.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And it requires continuous effort and dedication from all of us, working hand-in-hand with the Government, healthcare professionals, educators and community partners.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I once had a student named Sarah, not her real name, who struggled with severe anxiety.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Through early intervention, dedicated support from her teachers and her family's unwavering love, Sarah overcame her challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, she is a thriving young woman, passionate about advocating for mental health awareness.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Her story is a testament to the transformative power of understanding, empathy and timely intervention.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a reminder that, together, we can create a society where everyone has the opportunity to flourish regardless of the challenges they may face.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As we work toward this goal, let us channel our collective passion, energy and commitment to ensure that mental health remains a priority on our national agenda.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay): The Healthier SG initiative is testament to the Government's unwavering commitment to the health of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Recently, Minister Masagos, in his speech at the M3 Healthy Investment Family Festival, underlined the importance of addressing health challenges directly and investing in preventive measures for a healthier future.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I fully believe that the Healthier SG initiative will improve our community's well-being significantly.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I had previously shared my efforts to achieve a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By encouraging regular health screenings, we can detect health problems earlier and prevent their condition from becoming chronic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Apart from health screenings, the Healthier SG initiative can improve our community's well-being by promoting a healthier diet, exercise and mental wellness.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge community leaders to work closely with grassroots organisations and residents to develop a health programme that suit the unique needs of their respective communities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: One example is the initiative by M3@Jalan Besar.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We are obligated to take care of our health so that we can prevent chronic diseases and lead a healthier life.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When we are healthy, we will be able to better support our families and communities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In English): Madam, in conclusion, let us be the voice for those who may be struggling in silence and let us be the agents of change that drive our nation towards a brighter and more inclusive future, a nation where mental health and well-being is valued and supported.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As we move forward, let us remember that progress and success are not just about achieving individual goals.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Instead, we must work towards building an inclusive and compassionate society where every Singaporean, regardless of their background, has the opportunity to realise their dreams and contribute collectively to our nation's success and progress.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, let us stand together, united in our commitment to this refreshed meritocracy.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us continue to innovate, collaborate and co-create a brighter future for our children and future generations.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In the words of our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew, "A nation is great not by its size alone.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is the will, the cohesion, the stamina, the discipline of its people and the quality of their leaders which ensure it an honourable place in history." Let us honour his legacy by striving for a better, more inclusive, compassionate and resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some youths in other countries do not believe that they will be better off than their parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, many wonder if they can achieve their aspirations or will they be kept in the social class they were born into.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In countries where this hope has disappeared, the "have-nots" tussle with the "haves", there is a loss of unity and society is fractured, weakened.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And when the absence of upward mobility is overlaid with racial or religious fault lines, the social fabric frays quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must not let this fate befall us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In Singapore, we have kept social mobility alive across generations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to build a country where there will always be opportunities for families to better their circumstances and where their children have hope of a better and brighter future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Governments must always prioritise, invest in and preserve the social foundations of societies to provide a fair chance for everyone to move up in society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They must address the under-provision of at least three public goods: education, healthcare and housing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Society must accept policies that even out disparities to help address disadvantages families may face.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over decades, we have built a strong foundation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We provide families with access to affordable education, housing and healthcare, enabling Singaporeans to pursue their aspirations and realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The story of Ibrahim cited by Dr Wan Rizal just now, is just one of many stories of Singaporeans that succeeded because of their education; and Sarah, for access to good health systems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Coupled with Government efforts to make Singapore attractive for investments, we enjoy economic growth and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, these have helped to uplift generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These fundamentals continue to undergird our strategy today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We continue to make significant investments into public education, affordable housing and quality healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is why Singaporeans continue to sit shoulder to shoulder and all can access quality healthcare at our public hospitals, and their children attend school together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Sustaining these policies across generations is no easy feat.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we have managed to maintain the provision and quality of these goods on an even keel, without ballooning social expenditures that, ultimately, the taxpaying public has to pay for.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, a strong sense of personal agency and industrious work ethic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For countries to be successful, its people must be earnest in pursuing their aspirations and work hard to earn their success.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: From the day Singapore became independent, we understood that no one owes us a living.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We had to work hard to get where we are today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This ethos is deeply embedded in our psyche.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singaporeans know this and respect those who have earned their success and similarly, want to work hard to do well for themselves, their families and communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is this spirit that will propel this country forward amidst headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, those who have done well giving back to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have seen this in Singapore's early years where philanthropists and businesses raised funds and set up hospitals and schools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The community contributed to those in need among them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As our country prospered, we saw more individuals and companies giving back to society and uplifting others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must keep this spirit of giving back alive.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Giving back to society is a key ingredient of our country's success, where those who have done well acknowledge the role society has played in enabling the person to succeed and find ways to benefit others and help others succeed too.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As I said five years ago, this is how meritocracy can be moral: when the successful demonstrate a sense of duty to society, when they share the fruits of success with others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And importantly, we all must work together for the common good.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must never underestimate the power of working together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When different entities can come together and work in sync towards a common goal, we can achieve a great deal.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is this quality of private, people and public sectors working together that helped us pull through during the pandemic and remain united.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Not pulling in different directions and, ultimately, undermining society itself.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we will give all children a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are convinced by evidence that investments in the early years build a strong foundation in our children's lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why we have invested significantly in affordable and quality preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are also providing more intensive support to support mother and child early on in life, through KidSTART.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do not wait for families to come forward.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Instead, we reach out to parents as early as during the mother's pregnancy and work with a team of healthcare and social service professionals, volunteers and community partners, to support these children to give them strong chances early in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This prevents disparities in the early years from snowballing into greater disparities down the road.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It gives us the best chance of setting children up for success and is more effective than tackling issues downstream.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we will provide more support to families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the years, this Government has strengthened social safety nets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have provided transfers and subsidies and targeted assistance to those who need them most.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have designed schemes to keep people in employment and ensure wage growth.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will be proactive, because we know we need to identify issues early before they snowball into larger issues so that one thing does not lead to another: a health issue does not become an unemployment issue of another family member, which, in turn, affects their children's education.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also ensure that lower-income families get the help that they need quickly and easily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ultimately, we want families to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility – the three "S"es.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To do so, we will ensure our services are family-centric and easily accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is what ComLink sets out to achieve, by providing wraparound support for families with children living in rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ComLink is another programme that does not wait for families to come forward to get help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A befriender proactively reaches out to families to understand their various needs and aspirations and works with them to develop goals and action plans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Government agencies and community partners stand behind the befriender and work at the back end to coordinate suitable services and programmes for the families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As data is shared at the back end, families can receive assistance without submitting the same information to different agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will ensure that our social services are comprehensive, convenient and coordinated, so that families can get the help they need quickly and easily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, we will reinforce and support the personal agency of families who wish to improve their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many families want to secure a better future for their family and are taking active steps to uplift themselves and their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During our Forward Singapore engagements, some have suggested that we should find ways to encourage families who take positive steps, such as securing stable employment and ensuring that their children attend preschool, but to do so in a manner that does not erode their sense of self-reliance and personal agency.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When such families put in the effort, we know they are on the road to making progress in their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And as part of our social compact, it is good and right that we recognise such efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: So, we are studying how to do this in a bigger way, under ComLink.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Fourth, we want more social service partners across society to uplift communities across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Uplifting those in need goes beyond social services agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It involves businesses, community partners, neighbours and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We need partners to share their resources and know-how and distribute their social capital to uplift those who have less.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to harness the best of organisations to address the needs of communities in innovative ways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This means leveraging organisations' assets, expertise and networks to enhance opportunities for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, organisations can run mentorship programmes in their workplaces, widening the horizons of youths from less privileged backgrounds and inspiring them to work towards a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is timely, then, that many businesses are moving beyond traditional corporate service responsibility (CSR), to weaving social impact into their very core.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They know that their success is tied to the success of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Recognising their responsibility to the wider community, they are reshaping their businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Businesses know they are a better and more attractive company when they put equal emphasis on environment, social and governance (ESG).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They fulfil their social responsibilities from how they look after their employees, hire inclusively, to how they harness their businesses to make a positive impact on the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We need businesses to lead the charge and role model the ways in which they uplift communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will guide businesses in better measuring and expanding their social impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will celebrate and recognise businesses and other partners in this Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government will also do more to help private capital and family offices maximise their philanthropic impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our efforts, we must also tap on the best minds and translate the best research into practice to make a tangible impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am glad that many academics, researchers and IHLs have taken a keen interest in and are actively working to strengthen and support our families, from evaluating programmes that seek to ensure every child gets a good start in life, to examining ways we can enhance family resilience, so that our families can bounce back after setbacks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must tap on the wealth of knowledge and expertise at these IHLs to better and more effectively uplift our communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will strengthen our collaboration with academics and IHLs to improve policies, social work practices and the delivery of services to meet evolving social needs in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In my speech at the President's Address debate in 2018, I called for a Singapore brand of meritocracy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, I call on our IHLs, academics and researchers to conduct original research and build up a robust body of knowledge of social science that applies to our context, one that is made for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Everyone has a role to play in supporting those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of our refreshed social compact, we must find ways to benefit others and help others succeed and do well together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Individuals, families and our society will be better for it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is how an inclusive and caring society is built, by the hands of its people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will achieve much more when we work together than going in alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To better support families, we must join hands across society: businesses, social service agencies, community partners, volunteers and the Government working hand-in-glove.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I recall a family receiving five bags of rice from five different well-meaning social service agencies and corporates, which the family had no need for.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our hope is that, with ComLink, community resources can be better harnessed to fulfil real needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: What this could look like is: in each ComLink community, a volunteer befriender works with families to refer them to services, such as career coaches, to help them secure a job and nearby preschools and after-school programmes provided by the community to support the education of their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Rather than each of us going at it alone and duplicating efforts, let us synergise our various efforts into an effective national movement to better support families in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us cast our nets wider beyond our own sectors and work together in common cause to uplift those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us work together to keep social mobility alive in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay): Singapore must continue to be a country where there will be opportunities for families to better their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A country where they can fulfil their aspirations to secure a brighter future for their children and where our people believe that our brand of Singaporean meritocracy works.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To achieve this, we need a strong partnership across sectors, with each sector doing its part: the Government developing policies that help our people progress; the community harnessing available resources to address its needs; and volunteers bringing their skills and talents to uplift the lives of those around them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The mark of a strong social compact is when successful individuals give back to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We appreciate the efforts of our Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) who have long played important roles in uplifting the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many of our Malay/Muslim professionals have also stepped forward to serve and contribute to those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, Lawyers@M3 brings together lawyers, legal professionals and individuals with legal backgrounds to conduct talks on legal matters, Lasting Power of Attorney workshops and pro bono legal clinics for the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In their spare time, a group of soldiers also volunteer as mentors at ITE College East through Project Pathfinder, serving as role models for the students they journey with.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Muslim Healthcare Professionals Association also works with M3@Towns to bring health-related programmes and workshops closer to residential areas, to better benefit the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One of the traits that our community can be proud of is the progress that we made over the years, with the community and Government working together, by putting their minds and hands together to uplift the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The self-help group MENDAKI has become a model that many parties abroad are keen to learn from.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It was formed 40 years ago, at a time when our community leaders were concerned about the educational performance of our Malay children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They were committed to helping Malay children reach their fullest potential and attain success.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, MENDAKI remains relevant as it uses education as a key driver to uplift the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These MENDAKI volunteers understood our customs and culture and thus helped to augment the Government's efforts to improve Malay/Muslim educational outcomes in tandem with other communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is a meaningful achievement, as the 10 years of education provides the foundation to enable them to further their studies at the post-secondary level and enable them to pursue lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened by the progress made by the Malay/Muslim community, which was possible due to the awareness of the importance of education as well as the hard work and close partnership of all parties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us continue the efforts to enable our children to achieve their fullest potential.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, we must take reference from the latest findings from research and science.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The research shows that the early years are crucial to a child's development.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the decades, the Malay/Muslim community has made great progress on all fronts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes achieving stability, self-reliance and social mobility, while continuously giving back both to the community and to the nation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we face new challenges and as our society continues to grow and evolve, we will continue to work closely with community leaders, MMOs and our many volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will bring the community closer together to excel and uplift the lives of the most vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am confident that our Malay/Muslim community is well placed to forge ahead towards an even brighter future as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, let me conclude.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must be a society where Singaporeans will always have opportunities to forge a better life for themselves, regardless of their starting position.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must draw on the strengths of individuals and families, the social capital within our communities and resources from the public, people and private sectors to realise this vision.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I know we can because we are Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ahead of the 100th anniversary of Mr Lee Kuan Yew's birthday, let me share a quote which I think is evergreen, though he said it in 1965.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He said, "10 years from now, it will be better than now.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, it is immensely better than it was 10 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And it is ours, provided we have got enough sense to be together and nobody can keep an industrious people to work and fight for its future."

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.35 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.12 pm until 4.35 pm. ﻿Sitting resumed at 4.35 pm.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of our Forward Singapore conversation, much has been discussed about refreshing our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This has also been the central issue at this debate, including in the speeches of the President, Deputy Prime Minister Wong and various Members.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many have asked: what is a social compact?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, three "R"s – our responsibilities towards one another, how we reward work and distribute the fruits of our success, and how we relate to and respect one another.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Central to the Singapore social compact has been meritocracy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: People are recognised based on merit and achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We aspire as a nation for all to progress through our abilities, rather than birth rights, family connections or inherited wealth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It has spurred our people to excel individually.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It has allowed us to accomplish much collectively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, for a new country of immigrants, there did not and does not seem to be a better set of organising principles for people to operate within and excel.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of our forefathers came to Singapore because this was a place that allowed them to realise their dreams, despite their starting circumstances and lack of connections.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of us are also here today because of the opportunities afforded to us by this system of meritocracy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This includes Members from all sides of the House.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Other systems, such as aristocracy, plutocracy and nepotism, serve the interests of the few, rather than of the many.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These other systems would not have similarly motivated our people to aspire and strive, nor helped us to attract the best and brightest to commit their future to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While meritocracy has allowed us to avoid some of these pitfalls, it is now under stress worldwide.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are increasing questions if meritocracy is indeed fair or can it be fair, especially over the long term?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The process is also questioned by some who are unhappy with the outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To fix the problems, some real and some perceived, various countries have tried to fix the process in different ways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some countries have tried affirmative action for the less privileged groups – by levelling the uneven playing field in resources and opportunities for the less privileged groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It sounds fine, until we have to figure out who gets to decide who are the less privileged and what opportunities we should set aside for them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It becomes even more complicated when everyone feels relatively deprived or less privileged from their own perspectives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While meritocracy has generally worked well for Singapore so far, we also acknowledge that our system is not perfect.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must recognise that meritocracy, by itself, is not a panacea for all of our societal challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, as the world and our society evolve, our needs are constantly changing.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As society matures, those who have succeeded under the previous and existing metrics, will tend to want to perpetuate the same set of yardsticks – sometimes, to preserve their personal interests and comfort; and sometimes, they assume that what has worked will continue to work in a different future and do not think of alternatives that society may need going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must not allow any single, static and narrow metric to define success which can easily cause our society to stagnate and become irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The second danger of meritocracy, beyond competing on a static and narrow metric, is to reward success based on fixed, defined and pre-determined points in life and time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Once the determining test is conducted and the results are known, then it is as if the life trajectories of our people are fixed and become too difficult to change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: People develop at different paces and demonstrate different abilities at different times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This continuous meritocracy must extend beyond the education system, throughout life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Employers and society have as much a part to play to recognise the skills and talents of our people and not fall into the trap of credentialism of using any single dated metric.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must ensure that there is porosity in the ways that people can earn their spurs, contribute throughout life and allow them to bounce back from setbacks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The third danger of meritocracy is stratification over time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is natural and perhaps inevitable that the successful will tend to mix amongst themselves, creating exclusive social circles instead of sharing social capital.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is also human nature to want to pass on our wealth and privileges to our children, be it through the accumulation of assets, like investments and property; or through access to additional education resources, like tuition.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But these natural tendencies risk creating an endowment effect in society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Meritocracy becomes harder and harder for the less privileged, as their relative start state falls further and further behind the privileged.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must not leave this unchecked, or this will progressively stratify society, undermining our cohesion and eroding our higher purpose to draw on the talents and capabilities from all in society, instead of the privileged few.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The fourth danger of meritocracy is the misplaced belief that one's success is attributed entirely to one's talent and hard work, without acknowledging the role that society has played in enabling the person to succeed; the need for them to give back, uphold the system and strengthen our society; and the need to continually push back against the forces of social stratification.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students will have the flexibility to pursue different subjects at different subject levels, which allows them to customise their learning in each subject to a pace suited for them, while developing other areas of interest.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This, coupled with our plans to leverage educational technologies, such as AI-enabled adaptive learning systems, will help to provide more customised learning experiences for all our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also broadening the pathways in which students can access their education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With more opportunities for Direct School Admission and aptitude-based admissions, our students will be able to pursue studies based on their passion and aptitude rather than purely academic performance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continually review our admission policies to ensure that our schools remain open and accessible for students from diverse backgrounds while balancing other competing needs, such as preserving community ties and maintaining a variegated education landscape, to cater to different students' needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will press on with our efforts to develop 21st century competencies in all our students so that they can thrive amidst constant changes in our world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our curriculum will continue to be refreshed regularly to meet our students' future needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to emphasise important life skills and free up time and space for schools to strengthen learning dispositions and holistic development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will allow our students to develop an empowering portfolio of skills that will serve them well in whatever they end up doing, including adaptability, resilience and the ability to think critically and inventively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To these ends, we need the support of parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As parents, we must welcome schools to have their unique value propositions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This can better cater to the diverse needs of our children and help them to realise their full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Hence, it is not necessary or meaningful for us to constantly compare why one school's offering may be slightly different from another's.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The more appropriate question is not "Is this a good school?", but "Is this a good or appropriate school for my child?" As parents, we must also not fall into the trap of allowing broader dimensions of merit to translate into greater pressure to chase down more and every yardstick to "beat the crowd".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must remember that broader dimensions of merit are meant to help our children fulfil their potential according to their diverse strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is not meant to provide more ways to compare our children with others in areas that are not suited for their strengths or interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must remember to teach our children that, it is more important to surpass themselves throughout life than to surpass someone else in an examination.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, we will continue to create more diverse education pathways to allow greater porosity throughout life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Building on efforts, like Full SBB, in MOE schools, our post-secondary and tertiary pathways will provide more flexibility to better support students' learning and progression.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, polytechnic students will be able to spread out their learning if they intend to pursue side interests or need more time to build up a stronger academic foundation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: ITE's enhanced curricular structure will cater to a diverse range of learner profiles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Those who graduate with a Higher Nitec can look forward to further upgrading opportunities, such as the expanded offerings of ITE's Work-Study Diplomas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, we will invest in our people throughout life – not just in the first 15 years when they are with us in our schools, but also for the next 50 years beyond our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our people will need to continually upskill and reskill across their lifetimes to evolve at their own speed, create new value and stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will intensify our efforts to help our people stay relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of the Forward Singapore exercise, we will announce more details in due course on how we intend to help our workforce to upskill and remain relevant throughout life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But the Government's efforts alone will not be enough.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will need the partnership of industry, the innovation of institutions and the growth mindset of individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Industries cannot wait passively for the perfect worker to be developed for them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They must be active partners in shaping students' interests and skillsets even before they enter the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Hence, I welcome more companies to partner our schools in our Applied Learning Programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: After that, industries must also be prepared to invest the time and resources to support our workers to upskill continually.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I can understand the challenges for industries to commit to the training of our workers, especially in uncertain times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But if we do not grow our own timber collectively, we will all be fighting over a stagnant talent and skills pool.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Public Service, as an employer, will lead by example in supporting our workers to upskill continually.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our IHLs will continue to innovate and enhance their programme offerings, including through work-study programmes and stackable modules that may be more suitable for mid-career Singaporeans who wish to upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, our people will need to develop a growth mindset and passion for lifelong learning to make full use of these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will need this whole-of-society effort to enable our people to stay relevant and our industries to stay competitive in an ever-more challenging environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Fourth, not only must we respect a variety of professions, we must also fairly reward and remunerate the "heart" and "hand" work that is commensurate with the "head" work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our society needs all these roles to complement one another to function well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must ensure that our special needs educators who serve in diverse and demanding environments are recognised and appreciated for their efforts and contributions and for the challenging work that they do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must also ensure that our special needs professionals have professional development opportunities, just like mainstream MOE teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, there should be much more cross-pollination of ideas and mutual support between the mainstream and special needs educator fraternity and, similarly, within the special needs education sector.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I hope to have the support of all Singaporeans for us to move in this direction.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE and MSF will work closely with all our social service agencies to achieve this vision for the benefit of our special needs professionals and our special needs community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can achieve more collectively to better take care of the professionals in this sector instead of just thinking of optimising individually in respective institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond MOE, other workplaces that involve "hand" and "heart" work, including those in the essential services sectors, also need to play their part.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They need to hire, train and reward workers fairly based on skills and competencies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But we all know that this may translate into higher costs for some services provided by our fellow Singaporeans, which our society must be willing to accept and support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Otherwise, no matter how much we broaden the definitions of merit in our school system, none of it will ultimately work because it does not translate into tangible differences in earnings and at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Fifth, as a society, we must always do more for those with less to uplift the less privileged.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Everyone bears part of the responsibility, but those with more, bear more and those with less, get more.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why we want to do more for the less privileged in terms of housing, retirement adequacy, healthcare and many other areas.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This helps us to ensure that the gaps in society are not too stark, opening us up to the politics of envy and threatening the harmony of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It also helps us to avoid the need for affirmative action to decide who should or should not be given opportunities based on who they are rather than what they can do and what they can be.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, we must never degenerate into a system where everyone thinks they deserve more, relative to others.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, I see this as one of our major challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I fear a day when we constantly feel a sense of relative deprivation from seeing someone else getting more help than us, instead of feeling a sense of gratitude at being helped or feeling a sense of satisfaction at being able to help someone else.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will then lose our social cohesion to the politics of envy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Perhaps, we need to regularly remind ourselves that it is more blessed to give than if we are to just receive.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: A sustainable and resilient meritocracy is one where the largest possible number of people are enabled to achieve and contribute to take care of the fewest number possible who are unable to achieve as much.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The ultimate measure of our success as a society is not how many people we can help because they are unable to keep up but how few people we need to help because we have enabled them to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Sixth, we need to imbue the right values in all our people from young so that they can grow to become individuals who are willing to give back to society and create more opportunities for others.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All of us must recognise that our individual success is never just due to our own abilities and hard work, that without the opportunities that society provided us and the help from others along the way, we may not be where we are here today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: So, even as we celebrate and enjoy the fruits of our own labour, we must not forget to give back to society and others around us, to share the networks and ties that have helped us so that others may also similarly benefit from the opportunities and access.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, our schools already facilitate this sharing of social capital across different schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through cluster-based programmes like co-curricular activities, Values in Action (VIA) initiatives and other holistic development programmes, students from different schools can come together, get to know one another, learn how to communicate and collaborate with one another and form friendships that go beyond their own schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can do more of these through co-curricular activities, VIA programmes and even selected curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We encourage everyone in society to partner us in these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Show our students the way forward and help to nurture a more giving generation in time to come.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is something that all of us who have gone through the system and succeeded can and should do.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some may ask, what can I contribute if I am not as successful?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If I did not come from a school with a more illustrious history?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If I do not earn a big salary, wear expensive clothes, live in a big house or drive a fancy car?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: My answer is simply this: those material achievements are not the only yardsticks of success, nor should they define our ability to contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Neither should they determine the respect and dignity that one deserves.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we must define success by how much we contribute to others and the greater good and not just how much we achieve for ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We should have the courage to step up and say, "I can always contribute something, according to my abilities, regardless of where I am in life".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And everyone can say that and can do something about that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I look forward to the day when our society defines success not just by one's achievements but, more importantly, by one's contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When a true son and daughter of Singapore, who earns and deserves our respect, is one whose contributions not only commensurate with his or her achievements, but also one who contributes to the best of his or her abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In an increasingly volatile and uncertain environment, we need to avoid over-structuring our system and processes to give our people a false sense of security while eroding their development to handle an uncertain and untidy world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we must provide multiple pathways with diverse metrics of success while equipping our people with the life skills they need to thrive in the 21st century, to allow our people to chart their own way forward according to their own strengths and talents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In an increasingly competitive world, we can easily fall into the trap of always looking at the right side of the bell curve and feeling eternally inadequate.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we must remind ourselves of our gifts and responsibilities to help those who are less privileged than us.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Do not be taken by hubris to think that we have "arrived" or can ever "arrive" and need not evolve or improve anymore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We understand the merits of our system and how far it has helped us to come this far as a society by unleashing our potential as individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yet, we are not complacent to think that we can ever stop improving our system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Any living system that does not grow, will wither.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One group of Singaporeans which I would like to appeal for more support is families with autistic children, in particular, those from the lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Experts think that our high rates are partly due to greater detection from higher awareness and testing and, if data from developed countries, like the US, is an indication, we may detect more cases in the future.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, it is important that the Government expedites the set-up of a national infrastructure to provide holistic support for Singaporeans with autism, from diagnosis to end of life.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) can or may ramp up public education efforts to increase awareness among parents to diagnose their children as soon as possible if they notice the symptoms.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Parents should be reminded to follow up with their children's developmental milestone checks at polyclinics, clinics or hospitals.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Upon diagnosis, these children need to be given sufficient treatment and therapy at the optimal frequency to give them the best chance to develop to their highest potential.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is an essential and the best investment we can make in them, especially during the small window period when they are young, which will yield good progress and benefits over the long term.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Parents should also be provided with comprehensive advice by an appointed Government agency on how to navigate our system for the best care and protection for their children.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They must not be discriminated against for unrelated risk factors, which is the most common and longstanding complaint.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For low-income families, we must ensure that the treatment is affordable to them and provide the appropriate subsidies so that they will be able to keep up with the therapy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Counselling and adequate support should also be provided to the family members who often suffer from caregiver fatigue and burnout as well as depression.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need more activity and care centres for children and adults with autism to engage them and allow family members to work with peace of mind and caregivers to take regular breaks.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For lower-income families, the lack of capacity in these centres often mean that someone in the family – often the mother – would not be able to work because she becomes the caregiver.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is a blow to their household income, plunging them into deeper financial difficulty.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Autism lies on a spectrum, so while there are those who will be able to work and live independently, there are others are not able to do so.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need to establish care arrangements for them when their ageing parents and families are unable to continue taking care of them, especially the financially disadvantaged ones.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As sudden changes to their routines can be distressing for them, advance planning is important.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The preparation includes introduction and exposure to facilities, environment settings, volunteers and care professionals as well as financial arrangements and legal documentation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Next, I would like to appeal for more support and assistance for our SMEs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are many schemes and grants available, but some business owners have trouble navigating and understanding the processes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are confused by the red tape and even need external consultants to advise them on what they are eligible for.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, the owners and consultants' own interests do not always align, as the consultants' earnings are based on certainty and quantity of their commissions.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Accessible, timely and neutral advice from knowledgeable agency staff would make a very big difference.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the President noted in her Address, Singapore will face more resource constraints – land, labour and carbon – in the near future.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In addition, governments of major economies are providing support to boost their own industrial bases.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There will be a greater drive for nationalistic projects.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the Government consider publicising and sharing more about companies tapping capabilities in the IHLs as well as the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) and engaging on platforms, such as the Global Innovation Alliance?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help to raise awareness, inspire and encourage more Singaporeans to consider entrepreneurship.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore is working hard to attain food resilience and the Government is stepping up investments in food R&D, such as aquaculture, urban agriculture as well as alternative proteins.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is an appropriate and important sector for our SMEs to participate in.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need to increase local demand so that the cycle of local supply and demand is sustainable.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
